newsitem.title: USA: Delta Air seen naming Leo Mullin CEO - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: Delta Air seen naming Leo Mullin CEO - WSJ.

text.p: Delta Air Lines is expected to name Unicom Corp vice chairman Leo Mullin as its new president and chief executive on Friday, the Wall Street Journal reported.
The move will be the first time Delta named a new chief executive from outside the company, the paper said in its electronic edition.
The move is also a sign the company, which has long exhibited a cautious and insular culture, indends to reshape itself, according to the paper.
Mullin, 54, is not expected to be named Delta's chairman, the paper said.
He would replace long-time chief executive Ronald Allen, whom Delta forced out of his job last April.
